detail: GET /workspaces/4/projects/24/datasets/54/dataviews/76/pipeline/checkpoints/2 -> HTTP 500, empty response_body:{}, request_id:null, backend code: none surfaced (generic api_error/500). Reproduced immediately after view.checkpoint.create returned checkpoint_id:2 on our own view 76/dataset 54/project 24. Alternative input tried: omitted dataset_id from --input (letting CLI discover the parent) -> identical HTTP 500 on the identical endpoint/method, so the failure is not sensitive to input shape; this is a read (GET) with no body, ruling out a client-built-payload cause. Matches write-sweep-20260918 result exactly (view 73/checkpoint 1, project 21).

PATCH .../pipeline/checkpoints/2 -> HTTP 500, empty response_body, request_id:null, code:outcome_unknown (CLI correctly refused to claim success per its own hint: do not replay). Exact input matches the documented runnable_example (path:approve). Alternative tried: same checkpoint, different patch path enable instead of approve (still op:command, value:null) -> identical HTTP 500 on the identical PATCH endpoint. Since two different patch bodies (approve, enable) both 500 identically with an empty body, the failure is in the PATCH route itself, not in a specific op/path value -- rules out a client-input cause. Could not independently verify checkpoint 2 final state because view.checkpoint.get on the same view/checkpoint also 500s (see view.checkpoint.get finding) blocking reconciliation entirely.

PATCH .../pipeline/data-checks/3 -> HTTP 500, empty response_body, request_id:null, code:outcome_unknown. Reconciled via view.data-check.get 76 3: enabled still true, updated_at still null -> patch did NOT commit. Alternative 1 tried: op:replace,path:enable (no value) -> HTTP 400 4GENR007 'patches.0.value: Field required'. Alternative 2: op:replace,path:enable,value:null -> HTTP 400 4GENR007 "For op PatchOps.REPLACE, path must be one of [DataCheckPatchPath.SPEC]" -- this backend validation message proves op:command is the ONLY schema-legal combination for path:enable, so there is no alternative client input that avoids the 500: the single valid request for this op is the one that crashes the server.

POST .../derivatives/4/data -> HTTP 500, empty response_body, request_id:null, code:outcome_unknown. Input is the documented runnable_example verbatim (condition:{FILTER_TYPE:SHOW}) against our own freshly-created derivative id 4 (SUM of column_1/store_id) on view 76. Read-shaped POST, so no state to reconcile. Alternative tried: richer condition with STRING_PROP filter (COLUMN:column_2,OPERATOR:CONTAINS,VALUE:Store) -> identical HTTP 500. A third probe, empty body {} -> different HTTP 400 4GENR007 referencing a bare 'data' key (looks like an unhandled server-side KeyError message, not a real field name) confirming the route does inspect the body but breaks specifically once a well-formed condition is supplied. Two different valid-shaped condition bodies both 500 identically -> not input-shape sensitive, rules out client cause.

CLI accepts the request (exit 0, job 358 accepted on POST /dataviews/76/actions), but job get 358 -> status:error, response:{"error":{"message":"'destination'"}} (a raw Python KeyError repr, not a structured message) -- matches the item exactly. Alternative tried: target_properties.destination:local added explicitly (item's own text) -- same failure. Checked schema get view.export.create: target_properties for csv_file resolves to $defs.export_spec__S3TargetProperties, whose declared properties are only file/file_type/include_hidden/is_format_set/use_format -- 'destination' is not a documented field anywhere in the export_spec schema, so there is no schema-legal way for the client to supply it; the backend's own error message references a field its own request contract never exposes. Diff via typed route: view export csv 76 (confirmation:none, no export_spec needed) succeeded immediately and wrote a real 20-row CSV (dataview_54_76_export.csv, matches source stores.csv). view export list 76 54 returned exports:[] both before and after -- the generic route's failed action is not a persisted export config, so there is nothing to diff there; the real diff is schema-level (S3TargetProperties has no destination field) not list-level. Conclusion: view.export.create with handler_type csv_file is backend-broken; view.export.csv is the correct, working alternative and should be documented as such (client_docs angle already captured in recipes/exports.md).

POST .../pipeline/task_preview -> HTTP 400 5GENR010 UNKNOWN_ERROR 'Unknown error occurred. Please contact support.' wrapping error_object {code:720,message:'Source column not present.'}, request_id:null. Reproduced verbatim with the documented runnable_example (COPY:{}). Alternative tried per brief: COPY:{SOURCE_COLUMN:'column_1',NEW_COLUMN_NAME:'store_id_copy'} using the INTERNAL name (column_1=store_id, confirmed via view list 76) instead of the display name 'store_id' -> IDENTICAL error (same code:720/5GENR010). Per the brief's own test, this rules out the display-name-vs-internal-name docs hypothesis: switching to internal names did not fix it, so this is not simply a docs gap. Two things are true regardless of COPY field names: (1) task_spec is fully freeform (schema: additionalProperties:{} type object) with zero field-name guidance for COPY or any task type -- the CLI/schema genuinely cannot tell an agent the right keys; (2) independent of whatever COPY's exact keys should be, the backend wraps a specific, real, structured validation error (code:720 'Source column not present') inside a generic 5GENR010 'contact support' envelope instead of surfacing it as a normal 400 validation error the way other routes do (e.g. 4GENR007) -- that mislabeling is itself a backend response-shaping defect. Classified backend for the UNKNOWN_ERROR mislabeling; whether some other undocumented COPY key name would succeed is UNVERIFIED (task_spec's freeform schema gives no way to discover it without backend source, which was out of scope to read).

POST /workspaces/4/projects/24/datasets-from-pdf. Attempt 1 (file_name only, no table_list/is_preview_needed) -> HTTP 400 4DSET053 MUST_PROVIDE_TABLE_LIST_OR_PREVIEW (clear, actionable, reproduced verbatim). Attempt 2 added is_preview_needed:true on the provided fixture sample.pdf (a minimal synthetic PDF with plain text, no drawn table lines) -> HTTP 400 4DTSTO003 PDF_TABLES_DATASET_CREATION_FAILED 'Unexpected errors while creating datasets of pdf tables', request_id:null. Alternative input tried: hand-built a SECOND pdf (sample_table.pdf, file id 57) containing an actual vector-drawn 3x4 grid (m/l/S line operators forming real table cell boundaries) with aligned cell text, to rule out 'no real table in synthetic content' as the cause -> uploaded as file 57, ran create-from-pdf 57 with the same is_preview_needed:true -> IDENTICAL HTTP 400 4DTSTO003 PDF_TABLES_DATASET_CREATION_FAILED. Since a genuinely tabular PDF (real grid lines, not just text) fails with the exact same generic, non-diagnostic error as the trivial text-only PDF, this rules out 'bad fixture' as the sole explanation: the route either cannot parse either PDF's structure or the underlying table extractor is broken/misconfigured on release, and its error message gives zero actionable diagnostic information either way (no line/page detail, no distinguishing between 'no table found' and a parser crash). Classified backend given a structurally-real table PDF still fails identically.

POST /dashboards/v3/templates -> HTTP 500, empty response_body, request_id:null, code:outcome_unknown. Two different request bodies against the same freshly-created, valid blank dashboard both 500 identically with an empty body -> rules out a client-input cause; matches dashboard-reverify-20260918 finding exactly (both of ITS attempts also 500'd and did not commit).
